title: The Stripe webhook is a named no-principal route that verifies its signature
description:
**Phase 3 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** nothing
- **Runs in parallel with:** the checkout story
- **Unblocks:** every other story in this epic

---
Stripe calls with no Chatticus credential, so like the waitlist endpoint this route sits outside the principal marker system and must be named explicitly in NO_PRINCIPAL_ROUTES.

The signature is the whole security model. This route can enable an organization — approving recurring spend and unlocking a workplace — on the strength of a POST body. An unverified webhook is a public endpoint that turns on paid accounts.

**Done when:** the scenarios exist and fail for the right reason.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Feature: Paid enablement

  Scenario: The Stripe webhook is outside the principal system
    Given the thin-turn front door
    Then "/stripe/webhook" is a named no-principal route

  Scenario: An unsigned webhook is refused
    Given a Stripe webhook payload with no valid signature
    When it is delivered to the webhook route
    Then the response is 400
    And no organization status changed

  Scenario: A replayed webhook changes nothing twice
    Given a signed Stripe event that has already been processed
    When the same event is delivered again
    Then the response is 200
    And no organization status changed
